title: Efficiency Boundary for Risk Differences with Rare Endpoints and Rough Propensity
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; independent validity gate confirms mathematically sound below-floor result.
gap_reasons: Its substantive scope is a known uniform scalar covariate law, fixed Hölder exponent one-eighth, and two-sided scale-proportional risk bands, limiting its reach beyond this benchmark.
paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier field is capped at subfield.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved direct canonical and stipulated empirical-score boundaries, cyclic quadratic attainment, variance consistency, and feasible Gaussian inference. The math review passes with both cited leaves verified-attested; no Lean formalization was launched. The package remains below the field floor, with two editorial decision-panel findings preserved and no material in-scope strengthening available.
tldr: On the entire known-uniform-covariate rare-Bernoulli causal class with unknown positive Hölder-one-eighth propensity and normalized risks, uniform canonical efficient influence approximation exists, subject to \(nq_n\to\infty\), exactly when \(nq_n^2\to0\). A total original-record cyclic quadratic estimator attains the boundary with a positive relatively consistent variance estimate and uniform studentized Gaussian inference. A direct score-aware mixture obstruction excludes every Borel original-record estimator on violating subsequences. The stipulated full-score criterion is retained and has the same boundary; its score and the canonical score are generally unequal at fixed \(q\). Generic higher-order corrections, rare-risk variance calculations and sample recombination are credited.
gap: Corrected Robins gives ordinary efficiency above the fixed-risk smoothness elbow; the 2009 affinity theorem concerns deterministic functional targets. Neither inspected result supplies the full-class shrinking-risk empirical-score approximation boundary. DML imposes fixed positive covariance floors.
fill: Rarity-sensitive Hoeffding expansion, exact cyclic score recombination, and observable common-score subtraction provide complementary routes to a necessary-and-sufficient sequence theorem with positive feasible studentization.
